BackupFileOut.description:
One copy on the server (ADR 0034): a nightly one, the one before an upgrade, the one
Erase everything kept, or the database a restore moved aside.
BackupFileOut.title: BackupFileOut

BoxOut.description: One box to tick on a day.
BoxOut.title: BoxOut

ChangeOut.description:
What a change did: the series now (None when it was removed), the revision Undo
reverses, and how many one-off changes it had to drop.
ChangeOut.title: ChangeOut

ClearedOut.description: What Clear done took away, for Undo (POST lists/{id}/restore-items).
ClearedOut.title: ClearedOut

ClientInfo.description: How this device reaches Sunroom: About's URL (ADR 0034).
ClientInfo.title: ClientInfo

CopyWeekIn.description:
Copy a week's meals into another week (both the first day of a week). Spots already
filled in the target week are kept.
CopyWeekIn.title: CopyWeekIn

CountdownPatch.description: Only what's sent changes; an empty emoji clears it.
CountdownPatch.title: CountdownPatch

DayOut.description: GET chores/today: the Chores room, the Today panel's Chores today, Who's doing what.
DayOut.title: DayOut

EntryIn.description:
PUT meals/entries: with an id, that entry changes (its day and slot too); without one, it
goes into the spot (day, slot, position) and replaces what's there, if anything. A new text
is kept as a saved meal (or counts one more use of the saved meal with that name).
EntryIn.title: EntryIn

EntrySaved.description:
What PUT meals/entries did: the entry now, and what it replaced in that spot (for Undo:
put the replaced one back).
EntrySaved.title: EntrySaved

EventUpdate.description:
PATCH a whole series (``scope`` all) or, at an occurrence, ``this`` / ``following``.
``clear_rrule``/``clear_color`` say "remove it" (None means "leave it").
EventUpdate.title: EventUpdate

FakeEvent.description: Test server only: an event on a scripted calendar server.
FakeEvent.title: FakeEvent

FakeScript.description: Test server only: what a scripted server holds and does next.
FakeScript.title: FakeScript

HelperIn.description: Google's helper: the key file's text, uploaded once.
HelperIn.title: HelperIn

ItemPatch.description: Only what's sent changes. Empty text clears a note or quantity.
ItemPatch.title: ItemPatch

ItemsIn.description: One or several items ("Milk, eggs, bread" is split by the app).
ItemsIn.title: ItemsIn

LastChange.description: A list tile's last line, written out by the app: "Mia added Milk · 2:10 PM".
LastChange.title: LastChange

LibraryKindOut.description: A kind of library the screens offer, with what its fields say.
LibraryKindOut.title: LibraryKindOut

LibraryPatch.description: Only what's sent changes; a change of picks, limit or switch starts a pass.
LibraryPatch.title: LibraryPatch

LibraryPicks.description: What to show, by the library's ids: any pick matches, none means every photo.
LibraryPicks.title: LibraryPicks

LibraryTestIn.description: The test server's pretend library: ``wipe`` leaves it needing its key again.
LibraryTestIn.title: LibraryTestIn

ManifestOut.description: What the screensaver shows: every library photo not hidden or removed, newest first.
ManifestOut.title: ManifestOut

MealMoveIn.description:
Move an entry to another day (and slot); one already there takes this one's place
("Swap days").
MealMoveIn.title: MealMoveIn

MealsRemovedOut.description: Recently removed (7 days): entries taken off a day, and saved meals archived.
MealsRemovedOut.title: MealsRemovedOut

MoveIn.description: The drag fast path: to another day, keeping the time of day and the length.
MoveIn.title: MoveIn

PlaceOut.description: A town the location search found.
PlaceOut.title: PlaceOut

ReconnectIn.description: A new password (CalDAV) or address (a feed) for an account that needs reconnecting.
ReconnectIn.title: ReconnectIn

RemovedOut.description:
Recently removed (the last 7 days), newest first. Cleared items aren't here: Clear done
has its Undo, and the list keeps them as its history.
RemovedOut.title: RemovedOut

RestoreOutcomeOut.description: How the last restore went (it's applied as Sunroom starts again).
RestoreOutcomeOut.title: RestoreOutcomeOut

RestoreSummaryOut.description: What the chosen file holds (Restore from a File?).
RestoreSummaryOut.title: RestoreSummaryOut

RoutineRunOut.description: A child's routine on a day: its steps, what's checked, and whether its window is open.
RoutineRunOut.title: RoutineRunOut

RoutinesOut.description: GET chores/routines: the routines as made in Settings, and each child's day of them.
RoutinesOut.title: RoutinesOut

SavedMealPatch.description: Only what's sent changes; an empty emoji or link clears it.
SavedMealPatch.title: SavedMealPatch

SaverSettings.description: The plugin's settings as the wall uses them.
SaverSettings.title: SaverSettings

TodoOut.description:
The Today panel's To do: items still open that are due on the day or before, the oldest
first.
TodoOut.title: TodoOut

UpcomingOut.description: One thing coming up: a countdown, or a person's birthday (from their birthday in Family).
UpcomingOut.title: UpcomingOut

WaitingOut.description: A completion waiting for a parent's OK.
WaitingOut.title: WaitingOut

WeatherOut.description:
``status``: ok (a forecast, maybe stale), no_location (Settings → Household → Location
isn't set), waiting (set, nothing fetched yet), error (nothing to show, ``message`` says
why). With ok, ``message`` is why the last check failed while the last forecast shows.
WeatherOut.title: WeatherOut

WeekOut.description: GET chores/week: seven compact rows per column, the fridge-chart view.
WeekOut.title: WeekOut

get.description:
Data Only (Settings → Backup → Download, ADR 0034): a checked copy of the database made
now, not the newest nightly one, so it holds what was added today.

507.description: Not enough free space for the database copy

get.description:
Download everything (PLAN §13.7): the database, the photos and a manifest in one zip,
streamed as it is written. Settings → Backup calls it Data & Photos.

507.description: Not enough free space for the database copy

delete.description:
Remove one copy (ADR 0034). Never from a paired screen, as Erase everything: it can't be
undone, it's never urgent, and a parent's grant outlives the parent at the wall.

get.description: One copy on the server, any of the four kinds.

post.description:
Erase everything and start over (meta/erase.py, ADR 0029): a parent, on a signed-in
device, with the household password. Never from a paired screen, which a child can reach.
The password is checked as at sign-in, wrong tries counting against the same limiter.

The household password, asked before something that can't be undone happens off this
server: a wall screen uninstalling Sunroom and the family's data from the computer it runs on
(This Screen's Uninstall, ADR 0042). A parent's (on a wall, behind the PIN), checked as at
sign-in, wrong tries counting against the same limiter.

delete.description: Keep everything: the file sent is forgotten.

post.description:
The file itself is the body (as a photo upload's is), with its name in X-Filename. It is
checked and kept, ready to restore; nothing changes yet.

Restore the file sent, with the household password, checked as at sign-in and as Erase
everything does (the same bar: what's on the server now survives only as a copy).
Check now (About's button), at most once a minute.

put.description: "Name this screen" right after pairing, or a phone's own name.

post.description:
Sign in a new device with a code from a signed-in device. Wrong codes count as wrong
passwords do, so codes can't be guessed.

Add a Device: a one-time code another phone, tablet or computer signs in with. On a wall
screen, which anyone in the house can reach, only a parent may make one.
A parent's phone claims the code the screen shows.

post.description: Typed on the screen itself, when no phone is at hand.

put.description: Who's using this device? A wall screen is everyone's: it picks a person per action.

Set or change the PIN. Where the PIN is what made this device a parent (the wall screen, a
child's phone), changing it asks for the current one; a parent's own phone doesn't need it, so
a forgotten PIN can always be reset from there.

post.description: End this device's parent grant now (the display's Lock button).
A correct PIN unlocks parent things on this device for 10 minutes (no sliding).
